subagent_reports.topic: Discovery opportunity scout: executive summary quality, caveman voice contribution, spec-vs-test routing

sources.label: adv-review.md Persist Executive Summary (repo source)
sources.summary: Current durable executive-summary template: Outcome/Verdict/What Was Built/What Was Verified/Remaining Concerns/Consequence Context. No non-technical audience directive; 'What Was Built' pulls task implementation_summary verbatim, which is where technical changelog prose enters.

sources.label: command-voice-standard.md Voice Contract (repo source)
sources.summary: Repo-internal 'caveman-full' voice contract mandates 'uniform wording-density compression: drop fluff/hedging, technical terms exact.' Applies-to list includes 'Phase summaries', 'Progress reports and gate summaries'. Does-not-apply list does NOT exempt executive summaries. This ambient directive biases the summary-composing agent toward terse, jargon-preserving prose.

sources.label: advance-workflow spec rq-archiveVisibility01 (spec law)
sources.summary: Noise-reduction slice explicitly disclaimed executive-summary ownership: 'MUST NOT absorb separate active-change scope such as first-class executive-summary ownership; those remain coordinated boundaries.' No existing spec requirement owns executive-summary audience/plain-English quality — this change is the deferred coordinated home.

sources.label: Approval Consequence Context renderer (repo source)
sources.summary: 8-category consequence context (delivered_value first) is owned by a single programmatic renderer/model, spec-enforced against duplication. Provides an existing structural surface where 'delivered value / plain-English outcome' can be strengthened rather than adding a parallel prose block.

sources.label: workflow-noise-reduction-assets.test.ts (repo test)
sources.summary: Existing test bans 'Investment:'-style investment-report noise in archive/review/voice surfaces. New plain-English requirement must not reintroduce banned marketing-report framing; the two must be reconciled, not contradicted.

sources.label: Release-notes plain-language best practice (external, 3 corroborating sources)
sources.summary: Canonical model: tiered single document, outcome-first sentence ('what can someone now do'), then layered technical detail. 'Translation is not simplification; it is reframing — technical fact stays true, frame shifts from what changed in code to what changed for the user.' Directly supports proposal's translate-and-layer direction and Must-Not against vague marketing copy.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The reported symptom (terse technical changelog executive summaries) has TWO structural contributors, not one. (1) The adv-review Persist Executive Summary template lacks any non-technical audience/reframing directive and sources 'What Was Built' from raw task implementation_summary. (2) The repo-internal 'caveman-full' voice contract (docs/command-voice-standard.md) is an ambient compression directive whose applies-to scope covers gate/phase/progress summaries and does NOT exempt executive summaries — actively biasing the composing agent toward terse, jargon-preserving output. This is the specific caveman contribution the user asked to investigate: caveman is a real contributing pressure, but it is agent-facing runtime-prose compression, correctly aimed at handoffs/banners/verdicts; the defect is that executive summaries were never carved out as an exception. Routing: rq-archiveVisibility01 already deferred 'first-class executive-summary ownership' to a separate change (this one), so a durable advance-workflow spec requirement is the coordinated home — command-contract tests alone would leave the audience rule unlawed and re-driftable. The 8-category consequence-context renderer is the right structural anchor for 'delivered value' plain-English framing; reuse it rather than adding a parallel prose section. Note the caveman voice contract visible in THIS session's system prompt is a distinct GLOBAL user-config plugin (~/.config/opencode/instructions/caveman.md), out of repo scope; only the repo-internal command-voice-standard caveman scope is in-scope and actionable.

validation.notes: Proposal direction is architecturally sound and confirmed by external best practice and internal spec history. No blockers. Two coordination requirements: (a) explicitly exempt executive summaries from caveman-full voice scope in docs/command-voice-standard.md, and (b) reconcile with the existing anti-investment-report noise test to avoid ban-vs-require contradiction.

tradeoffs: Spec-law requirement adds durable governance but requires spec + doc + asset-test triad maintenance (higher ceremony than test-only).
Exempting executive summaries from caveman-full loosens uniform compression on one surface; acceptable because that surface's audience is non-technical approvers, not the agent.

Structural section-shape assertions resist regression but risk brittleness if they match exact prose; prefer structural/audience assertions over wording matches (consistent with existing rq-proseReduction structural-not-content test convention).

alternatives_considered.option: Command-contract/asset tests only, no spec law
alternatives_considered.rationale: rq-archiveVisibility01 explicitly deferred first-class executive-summary ownership to a separate change; leaving it unlawed re-creates the exact drift that produced the defect. Spec law is the coordinated home the prior slice pointed at.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a parallel plain-English prose block separate from consequence context
alternatives_considered.rationale: spec rq at spec.json:4291 mandates single-renderer ownership of approval consequence vocabulary; a parallel block duplicates and risks contradiction. Strengthen delivered_value framing inside the existing renderer/template instead.

alternatives_considered.option: Leave caveman voice contract untouched, only edit the summary template
alternatives_considered.rationale: The ambient caveman-full applies-to scope still covers gate/progress summaries and does not exempt executive summaries, so template guidance would fight an unstated compression directive. The exemption must be explicit to remove the structural bias.
Out of scope per proposal unless proven blocking. Not blocking: the reframing happens at summary composition, not at task-summary capture.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt spec-law route (advance-workflow requirement for executive-readable summaries) AND explicitly exempt executive summaries from caveman-full voice scope. Reuse the 8-category consequence-context renderer as the delivered-value plain-English anchor. Use structural/audience asset assertions, not exact-prose matching. Reconcile with the existing anti-investment-report noise test.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Route as spec-law requirement in advance-workflow (the coordinated home deferred by rq-archiveVisibility01), not tests-only. Two must-do coordination items surfaced by scout: (1) add explicit executive-summary exemption to docs/command-voice-standard.md caveman-full 'Does not apply to' list; (2) reconcile new plain-English requirement with workflow-noise-reduction-assets.test.ts anti-marketing-noise ban. Surface the caveman-voice finding to the user since they explicitly asked.
follow_ups: Design should decide whether the plain-English 'delivered value' lives inside the consequence-context renderer output or as a lead sentence in the executive-summary template Outcome section (or both).
Confirm whether the global ~/.config/opencode caveman plugin (session-visible, out of repo scope) should be noted to the user as a separate non-actionable contributor.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Draft design is boring-correct and high-leverage: strengthens existing spec/command/test anchors instead of building new subsystems. Spec boundary confirmed: rq-archiveVisibility01 body already carved out first-class executive-summary ownership as a deferred boundary, so a new rq-executiveSummaryAudience01 under advance-workflow is by-the-book placement. Renderer reuse confirmed: rq-approvalConsequenceContext01 already mandates a single renderer authority spanning executive-summary prose, so refusing a parallel 8-category model is spec-required, not just simpler. Caveman carve-out is a one-line edit to an existing Does-not-apply-to list. The Persist-Executive-Summary command template and two asset tests already exist to be strengthened, not authored. Single integration hazard: the anti-investment-report asset test bans marketing tokens on the same adv-review.md surface the new plain-English requirement edits; design already names this but should treat it as a hard test-design constraint.

validation.notes: All draft leverage points backed by located source anchors. No scope expansion beyond agreement. One coupling constraint (anti-investment-report test) must be honored during test design; already acknowledged in draft.

tradeoffs: Strengthening existing template and asset tests preserves locality but couples this change to the anti-investment-report test surface; banned-marketing and required-plain-English assertions must coexist on adv-review.md.
New rq-executiveSummaryAudience01 adds a durable anchor but adds one more spec.json to docs mirror pair to keep drift-test synced.
Caveman carve-out as a prose list line is structurally weaker than a code guard, but the protected substance is inherently prose, so a prose-plus-asset-test anchor is proportionate.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a parallel executive-summary release-context renderer
alternatives_considered.rationale: rq-approvalConsequenceContext01 mandates a single renderer authority explicitly covering executive-summary prose; a duplicate would violate spec law and fail its own tests.

alternatives_considered.option: Overload rq-archiveVisibility01 instead of a new requirement
alternatives_considered.rationale: That requirement body states it MUST NOT absorb first-class executive-summary ownership; those remain coordinated boundaries. A new requirement is intended placement.

alternatives_considered.option: Tests-only enforcement with no spec law
alternatives_considered.rationale: Agreement C4 and Agent Decision LBP1 require spec-law plus asset anchors for durable workflow behavior; prose/tests-only would drift.
Design DDC1 prefers small stable substring/category anchors; exact full-prose matching would be brittle and collide with caveman and anti-noise tests.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed with the draft design as-is. Elevate the anti-investment-report reconciliation to an explicit design constraint: new evidence-only wording must assert plain-English audience and decision-essential anchors without introducing tokens the noise test bans. Extend the two existing asset anchors rather than authoring new asset files. Add the caveman carve-out as one line under the Does-not-apply-to section.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Proceed with the draft design as-is; it is boring-correct and spec-aligned. Treat the anti-investment-report test reconciliation as a hard constraint, reuse buildApprovalConsequenceContext without modification, mint a new rq-executiveSummaryAudience01, and extend existing asset anchors instead of new files.
follow_ups: During planning, confirm manifest-doc-drift and checkpoint-surface-drift tests do not assert exact adv-review.md text that would conflict with the strengthened Persist Executive Summary template.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Design is a command-contract/spec/test refinement (no runtime data migration, no schema change), which matches the agreement scope and DONT4. Its authority layering (spec law defines behavior -> command docs operationalize -> asset tests anchor -> single consequence renderer) is sound and evidence-backed. Every material claim in Key Decisions verified against source: rq-archiveVisibility01 explicitly reserves executive-summary ownership as a coordinated boundary (Decision 1 correct); buildApprovalConsequenceContext is the single 8-category bounded renderer (Decision 3/DDC2 correct); adv-review.md already carries the hybrid summary shape to strengthen in place (Decision 2 correct); harden/archive carry-forward surfaces exist (Impl 3-4 correct); the investment-report-removal test exists and must be reconciled (Decision 6/DDC4 correct); command-voice-standard.md has existing carve-out slots for a narrow caveman exemption (Impl 5/AC4 feasible). One minor accuracy defect: the design lists 'human-checkpoints-assets' as a candidate regression anchor, but no such test file exists in plugin/src; the other three named anchors do exist. This is a non-blocking planning-precision issue, not a design flaw, and the design already hedges anchors with 'where possible'/'maybe'. Simplicity is good: it rejects tests-only (too weak for durable behavior per C4), a parallel consequence block (would duplicate the renderer), global caveman changes (OOS2), and schema changes (DONT4/OOS). No materially simpler viable alternative was overlooked. No existing spec requirement is contradicted; rq-archiveVisibility01 is complemented, not violated. Anti-marketing (DONT1) and evidence-only impact (AC2/DONT2) are treated as hard constraints reconciled against the existing noise-reduction test.

validation.notes: No blockers. Design is correct, spec-law compliant, and evidence-backed across all six key decisions. Single non-blocking accuracy nit for planning: 'human-checkpoints-assets' is named as a regression anchor but does not exist in plugin/src (verified via glob); prep should drop or replace it with a real anchor (human-checkpoints coverage may live under a different filename or a new test may be needed for AC5 archive/sign-off preservation). Existing verified anchors: approval-consequence-context-assets, workflow-noise-reduction-assets, adv-skill-backed-commands-assets.

tradeoffs: Spec-law + asset-test anchoring adds maintenance surface (new rq-*, docs mirror, structural assertions) vs prose-only, but satisfies C4's durable-behavior requirement and prevents drift.
Narrow caveman carve-out for executive-summary substance adds a policy exception that must stay scoped; overbroad wording risks exempting routine prose (design mitigates via narrow scoping + DDC3).

Strengthening the existing summary shape in place preserves the single renderer but couples plain-English rules to the same review/harden/archive surfaces, requiring reconciliation with the existing investment-report-removal test.

alternatives_considered.rationale: C4 requires spec/test anchors for correctness-critical durable behavior; prose/tests alone would leave workflow behavior unspecified and driftable.

alternatives_considered.rationale: That requirement's body (spec.json:918) explicitly reserves executive-summary ownership as a coordinated boundary; overloading would hide behavior in the wrong policy slice.
buildApprovalConsequenceContext is the single 8-category bounded vocabulary; a second block would fork the model and violate DDC2 and single-source-of-truth.

DONT4/OOS: no evidence these schemas block the executive-summary audience outcome; design correctly keeps them untouched.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to planning. documents.proposal:
# Proposal: Improve Executive Summaries

## Why
ADV executive summaries can currently become dense technical changelog prose. That fails release-approval use: non-technical executives need plain-English context about what they are approving, why it matters, what user/business outcome changes, what was verified, and what risks or follow-ups remain.

## What Changes
ADV should make executive summaries behave as release-approval decision surfaces for non-technical stakeholders. The workflow should guide agents to translate technical evidence into plain English, lead with release consequence and delivered value, and keep technical traceability as supporting evidence rather than lead prose.

This is expected to affect ADV workflow instructions and adjacent command/agent contract assets around review, harden, and archive sign-off. Discovery will determine whether spec law needs a durable requirement update or whether command-contract tests are sufficient.

## User Outcomes
- A non-technical approver can understand what they are approving without decoding engineering shorthand.
- A release sign-off includes plain-English context about delivered value, verification, risk, and remaining follow-ups.
- Technical evidence remains available for audit and traceability without overwhelming the executive-facing summary.
- Future archived changes avoid terse changelog-style executive summaries like migration numbers, SQL predicate names, and error-shape details as the primary explanation.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Improve the executive-summary authoring guidance used before acceptance and archive sign-off.
- Clarify audience, tone, and content layering for executive summaries.
- Preserve release evidence, verification, risk, and approval consequence context.
- Add or update tests/asset checks that prevent regression to terse technical changelog summaries.
- Determine during discovery whether `advance-workflow` spec law should gain a requirement for executive-readable summaries.

### Out of Scope
- Rewriting historical archived executive summaries.
- Changing task implementation summaries or sub-agent report schemas unless discovery proves they directly block the outcome.
- Removing technical traceability, evidence pointers, or approval consequence context.
- Adding a new dependency or external summarization service.
- Changing unrelated gate handoff voice outside executive-summary/release-approval surfaces.

### Must Not
- Must not replace audit evidence with vague marketing prose.
- Must not make summaries so long that approval context becomes hard to scan.
- Must not hide release risks, follow-ups, migrations, frontend impact, or rollback/ops readiness.
- Must not fabricate business impact that is not supported by proposal/agreement/task/review evidence.

## Affected Code
Likely areas from triage evidence:
- `.opencode/command/adv-review.md` executive-summary persistence and review-summary wording.
- `.opencode/command/adv-harden.md` release-readiness summary enrichment.
- `.opencode/agents/adv.md` pre-archive Change Report rendering guidance.
- Asset tests under `plugin/src/__tests__/human-checkpoints-assets.test.ts` and `plugin/src/approval-consequence-context-assets.test.ts`.

## Related Repositories
Current repository only: `advance`. `project.json` does not declare product-linked multi-repo scope.

## Constraints
- Keep the change implementation-free at proposal stage; discovery owns acceptance criteria and engineering detail.
- Preserve technical traceability through structured artifacts and evidence pointers.
- Keep summaries scannable and approval-focused.
- Follow existing ADV seven-gate workflow and command-asset test conventions.

## Impact
Release approvers should receive clearer, more useful context at the exact point they decide whether to accept or ship a change. Engineering teams retain auditability while reducing the chance that non-technical stakeholders approve unclear technical jargon.

## Context
Triage found the current durable executive summary template in `.opencode/command/adv-review.md` asks for a short narrative verdict and task implementation summaries but does not define a non-technical executive audience. Archive sign-off reads the artifact verbatim, so poor source guidance flows directly into release approval. External release-readiness and plain-language guidance supports a layered summary: decision and business/user impact first, verification/risk next, exact technical traceability in supporting evidence.

## Knowledge Gap Analysis

### Codebase unknowns
- Exact final set of command/agent surfaces that must carry the audience rule. Deferred to discovery.
- Whether tests should assert exact wording, structural sections, or both. Deferred to discovery.

### Ecosystem unknowns
- No external library or runtime dependency is expected. General plain-language/release-readiness guidance already supports the direction; discovery may cite it when shaping criteria.

### Domain unknowns
- Preferred strictness for summary length and section shape is not yet decided. Deferred to discovery.
- Whether executives should see a fixed section order or a flexible prose template is not yet decided. Deferred to discovery.

### Integration unknowns
- Whether `advance-workflow` spec law should gain an explicit requirement or command-contract tests are enough. Deferred to discovery.
- Whether harden release-readiness additions should be rewritten into the same plain-English layer or appended as a separate technical readiness block. Deferred to discovery.

## Discovery Agenda
- Decide whether executive-readable summary behavior is a spec-law requirement or command-contract/test requirement.
- Inspect review, harden, archive, and ADV sign-off assets for all places where executive-summary content is created, enriched, or displayed.
- Define a bounded summary shape that preserves verification/risk/traceability while remaining plain-English and scannable.
- Identify regression tests that enforce audience, layering, and non-jargon guidance without brittle prose matching.

## Discovery Findings

### Discovery Checklist
| Step | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Skill Discovery | PASS | `adv-instructions-audit` matched instruction/prose-anchor work and was loaded. No pending skill-review frontmatter found; only a documentation example of `review_status: "pending"` was matched. |

New finding: changelog intent already frames `executive-summary.md` as release-note/user-facing communication, but command guidance does not carry that audience forward. |
| Conflict Scan | PASS | No active overlapping changes. Validation warnings `NO_TASKS` and `NO_DELTAS` are expected pre-prep. Agenda has many unrelated planning follow-ups; scout added two related design notes (`ag-4i6FX5mV`, `ag-aA0B2zo7`). |
| Edge Case Investigation | PASS | Edge cases recorded below. |
| Design Question Depth | PASS | Open design questions annotated below. |
| Draft Spec Delta Shapes | PASS | Draft `rq-executiveSummaryAudience01` proposed below. |

| Completeness Verification | PASS | Full problem is broader than one bad summary: missing audience rule + raw technical inputs + caveman compression pressure. |

### Skills Considered
- `adv-instructions-audit`: loaded. Relevant because this is instruction prose backed by asset/spec tests.
- `customize-opencode`: considered, not loaded. This change affects repo-owned ADV command/agent surfaces, not user OpenCode config.

### Extends
- No relevant `temp/*.md` or `docs/*-prep.md` prior research found.
- Related existing intent: `CHANGELOG.md` describes `executive-summary.md` as a communication artifact for release notes, changelogs, and user-facing communication. New finding: current `adv-review.md` generation instructions do not preserve that audience.

  - `ag-4i6FX5mV`: decide renderer-vs-template placement for plain-English delivered value.
  - `ag-aA0B2zo7`: note global caveman plugin as out-of-repo contributor.

### Current State
- `adv-review.md:257-261` review display summary asks for one concise paragraph: verdict, finding counts, fixes, concerns.
- `adv-review.md:587-617` durable executive summary template has no audience rule; `Outcome` is 1-2 sentence narrative verdict; `What Was Built` uses task implementation summaries.
- `adv-harden.md:560-578` appends/replaces release readiness and consequence context, but does not specify executive-readable translation.
- `adv-archive.md:76-93` presents release signoff with approval consequence context categories and evidence rules.

### Edge Cases
1. Technical-only change with little user-facing value:
   - Summary must still explain why release matters in plain English, even if value is operational risk reduction.
   - Must not fabricate user/business impact beyond evidence.
2. Highly technical migration/security/runtime change:
   - Technical terms may be necessary, but must be defined or moved behind supporting evidence.
   - Risk/rollback/data impact must remain visible; plain language must not hide severity.
3. Caveman voice active in session:
   - Repo-owned caveman-full can compress needed context unless executive summaries are exempted or specifically layered.
   - Global caveman plugin is user config and out of repo scope; change can only document/avoid repo-owned conflict.
4. Regression-test brittleness:
   - Exact prose matching could make summaries formulaic and fragile.
   - Too-loose tests could pass while dense jargon returns.

### Open Design Questions
1. Where should the primary plain-English layer live?
   - Trust model: agent-owned technical decision.
   - Blast radius: wrong placement can duplicate consequence context or leave archive signoff unchanged.
   - Alternatives: executive-summary template lead section; approval-consequence renderer `delivered value`; both with clear ownership. Recommendation: both, with renderer owning category evidence and template owning narrative lead.
2. How strict should the section shape be?
   - Trust model: joint; user preference affects summary readability.
   - Blast radius: too rigid creates boilerplate; too loose allows regressions.
   - Alternatives: fixed headings, rubric-only prose, hybrid. Recommendation: hybrid fixed minimum headings with flexible bullets.
3. How should caveman-full interact with executive summaries?
   - Trust model: agent-owned with user-visible policy consequence.
   - Blast radius: if unchanged, compression pressure may keep causing terse summaries; if over-exempted, chat output may get verbose.
   - Alternatives: exempt all executive-summary artifacts from caveman-full; keep caveman but add detail requirement; exempt only archive signoff rendering. Recommendation: exempt executive-summary artifacts and release-readiness summary content from caveman-full while preserving scannability.
4. How much business/user impact may be inferred?
   - Trust model: joint; user decides tolerance for extrapolation.
   - Blast radius: unsupported benefit claims reduce trust.
   - Alternatives: strict evidence-only, allow bounded inference, or require explicit uncertainty. Recommendation: evidence-only with explicit “no direct user-facing impact” phrasing when needed.

### Draft Spec Deltas
- `rq-executiveSummaryAudience01` — Executive summaries are executive-readable release approval surfaces.
  - Given a change is ready for acceptance or archive sign-off,
  - When ADV composes or displays `executive-summary.md`,
  - Then the summary leads with plain-English release consequence and delivered value for a non-technical approver, summarizes verification/risk/follow-ups in scannable form, and places technical identifiers/details as supporting evidence rather than the lead explanation.
- `rq-executiveSummaryAudience01.2` — Caveman voice does not override executive summary substance.
  - Given caveman-full wording compression applies to runtime prose,
  - When an executive-summary artifact or release-readiness summary is composed,
  - Then compression must not remove required plain-English context, approval consequence, risk, or verification explanation.

### Related Pattern Scan
- Found related terse-summary pattern: `adv-review.md:261` one concise paragraph instruction for code-review display summary.
- Found related communication intent: `CHANGELOG.md:431` says executive summaries are for release notes, changelogs, and user-facing communication.
- No repo-wide `plain English` or `non-technical` rule exists today.
- No broad code-path scan beyond instruction/assets needed; this is a command-contract/instruction surface issue, not a runtime data-path defect.

### Completeness Verification
- Problem-completeness: high confidence. Evidence shows three contributors: missing executive audience rule, raw technical implementation-summary inputs, and caveman-full compression pressure.
- Solution-scope: high confidence. Intended scope spans creation (`adv-review`), enrichment (`adv-harden`), display (`adv-archive`/ADV signoff), and regression anchors (spec/tests/docs). No sole-entry runtime chokepoint claim is used.
- Secondary surfaces:
  - In scope: `adv-review.md`, `adv-harden.md`, `adv-archive.md`, `.opencode/agents/adv.md`, `docs/command-voice-standard.md`, relevant asset/spec docs/tests.
  - Out of scope: global `~/.config/opencode` caveman plugin config; historical archived summaries; unrelated gate handoff voice.

### LBP Check
Recommended direction matches long-term best practice: layered executive summary. Plain-English decision surface first; structured traceability and exact technical evidence remain available underneath. No external library/service is warranted.

Opportunity scout result: run. Five candidates considered; auto-adopt spec-law requirement and caveman-exemption direction; design-around renderer/template placement and anti-noise test reconciliation; surface global caveman as out-of-repo contributor.

### Recommended Objectives
1. Define executive summaries as non-technical release approval decision surfaces.
2. Ensure summaries lead with release consequence and delivered value, not implementation jargon.
3. Preserve verification, risk, follow-up, and approval-consequence evidence.
4. Clarify caveman-full does not compress away required executive-summary context.
5. Add durable spec/test anchors so the behavior does not drift.

### AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS — no ambiguity findings. Coverage: B:C F:C S:C M:C

## Clarify Resolution Log
- Q1 (resolved 2026-07-07T05:30:51+02:00): Minimum executive-summary content is “Decision essentials” — what changes, why it matters, verification, risk/follow-ups, and supporting evidence.
- Q2 (resolved 2026-07-07T05:30:51+02:00): Unavoidable technical terms may appear parenthetically; the summary should not require a full technical explanation for every term and should not ban technical terms entirely.
- Q3 (resolved 2026-07-07T05:30:51+02:00): Do not mention global caveman voice in the agreement; keep scope focused on repo-owned behavior and repo-owned caveman-full carve-out.

# Agreement

## Objectives

1. Make executive summaries serve as non-technical release-approval decision surfaces.
2. Ensure each summary explains decision essentials: what changes, why it matters, verification, risk/follow-ups, and supporting evidence.

- SC2: Each summary covers decision essentials: what changes, why it matters, verification, risk/follow-ups, and supporting evidence.
- SC3: Technical terms appear only as parenthetical support, not lead explanation.
- SC4: Repo-owned caveman-full policy no longer compresses away executive-summary substance.

## Constraints

- C2: Keep summaries scannable; do not turn executive summaries into long essays.
- C3: Keep this change current-repo scoped to `advance`; no product-linked or cross-repo scope is in effect.

## Avoidances

# Design

## Architecture Overview

This is a command-contract/spec/test change, not a runtime data migration. Add first-class executive-summary audience law to `advance-workflow`, then align the command surfaces that create, enrich, and display the artifact.

Authority layering:

1. `advance-workflow` spec defines durable behavior.
2. Command/agent docs operationalize that behavior at review, harden, and archive sign-off.
3. Existing asset tests verify stable anchors in command/docs/spec surfaces.
4. `buildApprovalConsequenceContext` remains the single structured release-consequence vocabulary; no parallel consequence model is added.

## Key Decisions

1. **Mint a new `rq-executiveSummaryAudience01` requirement.** Existing `rq-archiveVisibility01` explicitly leaves first-class executive-summary ownership to a coordinated boundary, so overloading that requirement would hide the new behavior in the wrong policy slice.
2. **Strengthen existing executive-summary shape in place.** `adv-review.md` already has a hybrid artifact shape (`Outcome`, `Verdict`, `What Was Built`, `What Was Verified`, `Remaining Concerns`, `Consequence Context`). The design updates its audience/content rules instead of creating a new artifact.
3. **Reuse the Approval Consequence Context renderer.** The renderer already owns the 8-category approval vocabulary and evidence bounds. The change should strengthen how summary authors use `delivered value`/context evidence, not duplicate the renderer.
4. **Carve out executive-summary substance from repo-owned caveman-full compression.** Caveman-full remains correct for routine chat/gate prose, but must not remove decision essentials from executive-summary or release-readiness artifact content.
5. **Keep evidence-only impact.** For internal or technical changes, summaries state operational/risk impact plainly and avoid unsupported business/user claims.
6. **Treat anti-investment-report noise as a hard design constraint.** Plain-English executive summaries must explain release context without reintroducing vague marketing or banned investment-report framing.

## ADR Drafts

None. Decisions are workflow-contract refinements with low reversal cost and no new external architecture.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Spec law**
   - Add `rq-executiveSummaryAudience01` under `advance-workflow`.
   - Include scenarios for: executive-readable decision essentials, technical details as parenthetical/supporting evidence, evidence-only impact, and caveman-full not overriding summary substance.
   - Update `docs/specs/advance-workflow.md` mirror.

2. **Review summary authoring**
   - Update `.opencode/command/adv-review.md` `### Persist Executive Summary`.
   - Require hybrid minimum sections/content: outcome, delivered value/why it matters, verification, risks/follow-ups, supporting technical evidence, and consequence context.
   - Direct summary authors to translate task/gate evidence into plain English before listing technical terms.
   - Allow unavoidable technical terms only as parenthetical supporting detail.

3. **Harden/release readiness carry-forward**
   - Update `.opencode/command/adv-harden.md` so release-readiness additions preserve the executive-readable layer and do not append dense scanner/report jargon as lead prose.
   - Preserve `harden evidence unavailable` semantics and release-owned category rules.

4. **Archive/sign-off display**
   - Update `.opencode/command/adv-archive.md` and `.opencode/agents/adv.md` only where needed to preserve and display the improved summary at Tier B sign-off.
   - Do not recompose historical summaries and do not add a second approval context block.

5. **Caveman policy**
   - Update `docs/command-voice-standard.md` `Does not apply to` or caveman composition rules to exempt executive-summary/release-readiness artifact substance from context-removing compression.
   - Scope carve-out narrowly: not general gate handoff voice, not global user-owned caveman config.

6. **Regression anchors**
   - Extend existing asset tests where possible:
     - `plugin/src/__tests__/human-checkpoints-assets.test.ts`
     - `plugin/src/approval-consequence-context-assets.test.ts`
     - `plugin/src/workflow-noise-reduction-assets.test.ts`
     - `plugin/src/adv-skill-backed-commands-assets.test.ts` if caveman composition anchors are the right locality.
   - Use structural substring/category assertions instead of full prose snapshots.

## LBP Analysis

Preferred long-term path: spec-law plus command-contract tests.

Why:

- The defect is not an isolated typo; it is a durable workflow-quality requirement that should survive future prompt edits.
- Existing specs already separate archive-visibility noise policy from executive-summary ownership, making a new requirement the clean home.
- Existing renderer and asset-test surfaces provide low-risk anchors; no runtime schema or external dependency is needed.
- Evidence-only impact and anti-investment-report constraints prevent the plain-English summary from becoming marketing copy.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Tests only:** too easy to drift because no spec law owns the audience requirement.
- **Parallel consequence context block:** duplicates the existing 8-category renderer and risks contradiction.
- **Global caveman config changes:** out of repo scope and user-owned.
- **Task/sub-agent summary schema changes:** not needed unless later implementation proves the summary authoring layer cannot translate existing evidence.

## Affected Components

- `.adv/specs/advance-workflow/spec.json`
- `docs/specs/advance-workflow.md`
- `.opencode/command/adv-review.md`
- `.opencode/command/adv-harden.md`
- `.opencode/command/adv-archive.md`
- `.opencode/agents/adv.md`
- `docs/command-voice-standard.md`
- `plugin/src/__tests__/human-checkpoints-assets.test.ts`
- `plugin/src/approval-consequence-context-assets.test.ts`
- `plugin/src/workflow-noise-reduction-assets.test.ts`
- Possibly `plugin/src/adv-skill-backed-commands-assets.test.ts` for caveman composition anchors

## Design-Derived Criteria

DDC1: Asset tests must assert stable anchors for non-technical audience, decision essentials, evidence-only impact, parenthetical technical terms, caveman carve-out, and traceability preservation without snapshotting full summary prose.

DDC2: Any Approval Consequence Context changes must preserve `rq-approvalConsequenceContext01`: all 8 categories, stable order, bounded rows, evidence pointers, no raw logs/diffs/task spam/full scanner reports.

DDC3: Caveman carve-out must be scoped to executive-summary/release-readiness artifact substance only; general chat/gate handoff prose remains under caveman-full voice.

DDC4: Plain-English requirements must coexist with the existing investment-report-noise ban; tests must prove both explanatory context and no vague marketing/investment-report framing.

DDC5: Verification should use targeted asset tests first, then broader repo checks per prep; no live plugin reload is required to prove command/spec asset behavior in source tests.

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Summary becomes vague marketing | Evidence-only impact, anti-investment-report constraint, DONT1/DONT2 contract checks |
| Summary hides technical risk or follow-ups | Required risks/follow-ups/supporting-evidence sections and preserved Approval Consequence Context |
| Duplicate consequence context | Keep `buildApprovalConsequenceContext` as single renderer; command docs display/preserve it |
| Tests become brittle | Structural substring/category assertions, not exact full prose matching |
| Caveman carve-out expands too far | Scope to executive-summary/release-readiness artifact substance only |
| Historical archived summaries accidentally touched | Explicit OOS and AC7; implementation should not run archive rewrites |

## Design Leverage Scout

- Trigger: run — workflow/spec/test design with multiple instruction surfaces.
- Candidates considered: 5.
- Auto-adopted: 4.
  - Mint new `rq-executiveSummaryAudience01`, not overload `rq-archiveVisibility01`.
  - Reuse `buildApprovalConsequenceContext`; reject parallel 8-category model.
  - Extend existing asset anchors where possible.
  - Strengthen existing `adv-review.md` executive-summary template in place.
- Surfaced/integrated: 1.
  - Anti-investment-report reconciliation elevated from mitigation to hard design-derived criterion DDC4.
- Inconclusive/skipped: none.

## Validator Notes

Validator result: pass / Validated.

Evidence cited:

- `rq-archiveVisibility01` reserves first-class executive-summary ownership as a coordinated boundary.
- `buildApprovalConsequenceContext` is the single 8-category bounded renderer.
- `adv-review.md` already has the hybrid executive-summary shape targeted by this design.
- `adv-harden.md` and `adv-archive.md` provide real carry-forward/sign-off surfaces.
- `workflow-noise-reduction-assets.test.ts` provides the investment-report-noise anchor.
- `docs/command-voice-standard.md` has existing carve-out slots for narrowly scoping caveman behavior.

Validator recommendation: proceed to planning. Keep caveman carve-out narrow and use the full existing asset-test paths during prep.
